item.title: Trump Administration Divide on China Policy Breaks Into Public View
item.description: The airing of a fight over advanced A.I. chips shows how much the Nvidia scandal has deepened fissures inside the government, just as President Trump heads to a critical meeting with his Chinese counterpart.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Swan, Maggie Haberman, Ana Swanson and Shawn McCreesh
item.category: Ministry of State Security of the People's Republic of China
Far East, South and Southeast Asia and Pacific Areas
item.media:description: President Trump acknowledged on Monday that the Treasury and commerce secretaries had been at odds over how hard to crack down on a loophole that has allowed China to access advanced A.I. chips through data centers in other countries.

item.title: Madison Huang, Jensen Huang’s Daughter, Became a Powerful Force at Nvidia
item.description: Installed as her father’s de facto chief of staff, Jensen Huang’s daughter alienated top executives. Now her lingering role poses a test for interim C.E.O. Colette Kress.
item.dc:creator: Kalley Huang, Tripp Mickle and Ryan Mac
item.media:description: Madison Huang, a senior director of product marketing at Nvidia and daughter of Jensen Huang, at the 2026 World Robot Conference, in Beijing in August.

item.title: Facing Criticism, Trump Administration Says It’s Investigating Megaspeed
item.description: The announcement appeared to be a response to recent criticism that the Commerce Department has moved too slowly on the alleged chip smuggling case.
item.dc:creator: Ana Swanson and Tripp Mickle
item.category: Ministry of State Security of the People's Republic of China
item.media:description: Megaspeed is a Singaporean firm that was created and led for a time by Alice Huang.

item.title: Debt Problems of the Richest Countries Are Trickling Down to the Poorest
item.description: The debt load of developing countries jumped to $9.4 trillion as high interest rates and other global shocks batter their economies.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Cohen
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Finbarr O'Reilly for The New York Times
item.media:description: A market in Daloa, western Ivory Coast. Ivory Coast, Kenya and Nigeria have pledged annual interest rates of 7.5 to more than 10 percent to lenders.

item.title: Shoe Prices Hit a Record High Amid Inflation and Increased Tariffs
item.description: Shoe prices hit a record high in October as brands contend with the rising cost of materials and increased tariffs.
item.dc:creator: Kim Bhasin
item.media:description: The jump in the price of shoes reached a record high this year as footwear companies pushed elevated costs on to American consumers.

item.title: Trump Will Miss Most of the ASEAN Summit
item.description: President Trump will arrive in Manila as the meeting is wrapping up, a sign of how U.S. policy has left the region balancing between Washington and Beijing.
item.dc:creator: Verena Hölzl and Jason Gutierrez
item.media:description: President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. of the Philippines speaking during the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit in Manila on Sunday. The bloc has come to see the United States as an unreliable partner.

item.title: United Airlines Flights Resume After ‘Widespread System Outage’
item.description: The brief disruption, after a nationwide ground stop last week, added to concerns about air travel ahead of a busy Thanksgiving travel period.

item.media:description: United Airlines said that “while some flights were delayed” by a “widespread system outage,” there was “no impact on flights in progress, or on United Express flights,” referring to its regional network of smaller carriers.

item.title: Chase Bank Resumes Normal Operations After ‘Software Bug’ Disrupted Transactions
item.description: After technical problems grounded flights nationwide and Microsoft products failed, the banking issues added to a sense of doom about the systems underpinning daily life.
item.dc:creator: Michael Levenson

item.media:description: J.P. Morgan Chase said in a statement it was dealing with a technical issue that was affecting its banking customers.

item.title: Pilots Kept Contact With Controllers During Nationwide Halt to Flights

item.title: Ukraine Attacks Kerch Bridge Linking Russia to Occupied Crimea
item.description: The attacks, far from the front lines, forced the only bridge between Russia and the occupied Crimean Peninsula to close. Traffic on two bridges in Kyiv was also stopped.
item.dc:creator: Marc Santora
item.media:description: The Kerch Strait Bridge in 2023. The structure is the only bridge linking Russia to Crimea, which Russian forces illegally annexed in 2014.
